slides.narration: Welcome to Book II, Chapter 23: Appendix B — Executable Ownership and Failure Labs. This deck follows the Chapter 1 Slides model: concept on the left, code or evidence on the right, and presenter notes that tell the instructor what to say and do. Modern C++ is not about using the newest syntax because it looks impressive. It is about encoding ownership, lifetime, invariants, generic behavior, and failure boundaries so the program is easier to reason about and harder to misuse.

Learners should be able to say what Appendix B — Executable Ownership and Failure Labs changes about program design, not merely identify a keyword. In modern C++, the evidence might be a destructor running, a copy becoming independent, a move leaving ownership in exactly one place, a constrained template rejecting a bad call, or an algorithm producing a predictable sequence.

slides.title: Requirement and model
keyPoints: A lease must release an acquired resource exactly once, including during exception unwinding.
A failed acquisition must not be counted as a live lease.
Moving a lease must transfer responsibility without duplicating it, and move assignment must first release the.
Repeated explicit close must be harmless under this class’s contract.
slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 23, treat Requirement and model as a design decision with costs and evidence. A lease must release an acquired resource exactly once, including during exception unwinding. A failed acquisition must not be counted as a live lease. Moving a lease must transfer responsibility without duplicating it, and move assignment must first release the destination’s previous resource. Repeated explicit close must be harmless under this class’s contract. The registry is a deterministic fake device with eight slots. It is not a wrapper around an operating-system handle API. Its counters make acquisition and release visible without relying on allocation addresses or external state. The registry owns the bookkeeping and must outlive every lease that borrows it. The lease owns responsibility for one slot, not the registry itself. A graduate-level explanation should say what the abstraction buys, what rule keeps it honest, and what artifact proves the rule: source code, compiler acceptance or rejection, stdout, stderr, exit status, object state, or a test witness.

slides.title: Requirement and model
keyPoints: Assigning a sequence must either produce an independent copy of the source values or leave the destination values.

Assigning a sequence must either produce an independent copy of the source values or leave the destination values.
slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 23, treat Requirement and model as a design decision with costs and evidence. Assigning a sequence must either produce an independent copy of the source values or leave the destination values unchanged. Copying can fail after zero, one, or two elements have been copied. The test uses a copy budget, not actual memory exhaustion, to make those failure points reproducible. Each cell stores an integer and a borrowed test policy. The source policy must outlive the source and its copies. The policy’s counter is outside the promised value-state boundary: it changes when copying is attempted. The sequence’s logical value is the collection of integers returned by snapshot, not the instrumentation state used to inject failures. A graduate-level explanation should say what the abstraction buys, what rule keeps it honest, and what artifact proves the rule: source code, compiler acceptance or rejection, stdout, stderr, exit status, object state, or a test witness.

keyPoints: The vector begins with reserved storage for three elements and then reserves beyond its current capacity.

slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 23, treat Evidence and interpretation as a design decision with costs and evidence. The vector begins with reserved storage for three elements and then reserves beyond its current capacity. This forces a capacity increase without relying on an implementation’s growth factor. The program prints the observed copy and move counts for the current compiler/library combination. Different valid implementations may make different choices within their contracts, so exact counts are not fixture expectations. The second part tests a direct move of the potentially throwing type. That type checks its rejection policy before changing the source value. Consequently, the failed direct move preserves the source under this class’s design. A later successful move sets the source value to zero. These outcomes are properties of the code in front of you, not a general promise that every throwing move preserves its source or every successful move empties it. A graduate-level explanation should say what the abstraction buys, what rule keeps it honest, and what artifact proves the rule: source code, compiler acceptance or rejection, stdout, stderr, exit status, object state, or a test witness.

slides.title: Evidence and interpretation
keyPoints: Two readers copy the owner of revision one.
Replacing the current pointer publishes revision two for future readers but leaves revision one alive for the.
Releasing the first reader is insufficient to expire the weak observer.
Releasing the final strong reader allows expiry, and locking the expired observer produces no owner.
slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 23, treat Evidence and interpretation as a design decision with costs and evidence. Two readers copy the owner of revision one. Replacing the current pointer publishes revision two for future readers but leaves revision one alive for the existing readers. Releasing the first reader is insufficient to expire the weak observer. Releasing the final strong reader allows expiry, and locking the expired observer produces no owner. The aliasing constructor then exposes the vector member of revision two while sharing the snapshot’s ownership group. Resetting the ordinary snapshot pointer does not destroy the enclosing object because the aliasing owner remains. The stored pointer and the owned object’s address need not be identical; ownership identity and exposed address are distinct concepts. A graduate-level explanation should say what the abstraction buys, what rule keeps it honest, and what artifact proves the rule: source code, compiler acceptance or rejection, stdout, stderr, exit status, object state, or a test witness.
